proposals.note: Removed the failed hypothesis (which claimed symmetry but failed verification). The previous high-risk proposals with many parameters and no symmetry (c0001, c0007) or failed symmetry (c0002, c0003) suggest that either over-parameterization or incorrect symmetry assumptions are detrimental. This proposal uses a standard 'Ring' entanglement topology (CNOTs forming a cycle) which respects the cyclic symmetry of the graph nodes if the feature map respects it (lexicographic order of pairs usually implies a fixed labeling, but cyclic shifts of nodes 0-5 map edges to edges in a specific way). However, since the verifier failed the previous hypothesis, I am dropping the hypothesis to focus on expressibility. The block consists of a linear chain of CNOTs, a layer of parameterized Z rotations, and a reverse linear chain of CNOTs. This is a standard, robust ansatz block. I have reduced the number of parameters to 6 (one per qubit) to avoid overfitting and reduce development risk, as seen in successful low-risk proposals like c0010 (2 params) and c0009 (3 params). The structure is simple and deep enough to capture correlations.
